changes_vs_current: New topic. Scope: authors of books (novelists, playwrights, poets, children's authors); philosophers/thinkers on the YouGov writer list (Plato, Freud, Marx) and comic writer Stan Lee left out. Computed order (average position over 10 people sources: YouGov fame merged rank over 44 authors, missing 49; Harris favorite authors 2015 and 2010 top 10, missing 15; WordsRated 2022 favorite authors top 25, missing 30; Harris favorite books 2014 and 2008 mapped to authors, missing 15; Wikipedia best-selling fiction authors top 25, missing 30; BookScan 2004-21 top 5, missing 10; Great American Read top 25, missing 30; Libby 2025 top 10, missing 15. Long lists were cut at 25 so that eligibility gaps in one list (no Shakespeare/Seuss/Poe in novel-only polls) do not swamp the average): 1 Rowling 5.3, 2 King 9.6, 3 Tolkien 11.2, 4 Patterson 12.0, 5 Harper Lee 13.9, 6 Austen 14.1, 7 Christie 14.4, 8 Fitzgerald 14.5, 9 Shakespeare 14.8, 10 Seuss 15.2, 11 Twain 15.9, 12 Steinbeck 16.0, 13 Steel 16.2, 14 Mitchell 16.7, 15 Roberts 16.9, 16 Alcott 17.4, 17 Grisham 17.4, 18 Koontz 17.5, 19 Clancy 17.9, 20 Orwell 18.0, 21 Dickens 18.1, 22 Poe 18.2, 23 Gabaldon 18.3, 24 Dickinson 18.5, 25 Hemingway 18.6, 26 Angelou 18.7, 27 Maas 18.8. Gut-check moves: (1) Stephen King 2 -> 1 and Rowling 1 -> 2: King is #1 in both general-public favorite-AUTHOR polls (Harris 2010 and 2015, where Rowling was 9 and 3), above Rowling on YouGov fame (92 vs 91) and well above on popularity (61 vs 53). Rowling's lead comes from favorite-BOOK polls where Harry Potter is one series vs King's spread-out catalog, and from self-selected WordsRated. (2) Shakespeare 9 -> 3, Dr. Seuss 10 -> 4, Mark Twain 11 -> 5: all three are in the gut check's top 5 and are the top 4 by YouGov fame with King/Rowling (Seuss 96, Shakespeare 95, Twain 91), Shakespeare is #1 in sales and Seuss #2 in BookScan; they rank low only because favorite-novel polls cannot include plays or picture books, and Twain is still Harris 2015 #8 and GAR 17. No naming/recall source puts them lower. (3) Poe 22 -> 8, Dickens 21 -> 9, Hemingway 25 -> 12: in the gut check; YouGov fame puts them 7, 6 and 11 (Poe and Dickens 90%, Hemingway 83%) and popularity 69%, 68%, 58%; YouGov 2017 has Poe as the most-read of ten authors (67%, ahead of Shakespeare 64%). The sources placing them lower are favorite-book lists (Dickens WordsRated 47/GAR 29, Hemingway WordsRated 87/GAR 65), which measure a favorite novel, not who people name; Poe is ineligible in those. Hemingway kept at 12 (last gut-check slot) because those favorite lists rate him weakest of the three. (4) Tolkien 3 -> 6 and Patterson 4 -> 7: moved down only by the lifts above; Tolkien is in the gut check and has 7 sources; Patterson has 7 sources (Harris 2/2, BookScan 1, Libby 2) but YouGov fame of only 73%. (5) Austen 6 -> 10 and Harper Lee 5 -> 11: both in the gut check and kept in the top 12; Lee's YouGov fame is just 61% (people know the book more than her name). (6) Christie 7 -> 13, Fitzgerald 8 -> 14, Steinbeck 15 ... Gabaldon 24 keep their computed relative order below the gut-check items. Emily Dickinson (computed 24) drops to first alternate because Hemingway moved into the 24. Diana Gabaldon stays at 24 on GAR #2 and WordsRated #17 (fan-driven; YouGov page not readable).
confidence: High for the top 5 set (King, Rowling, Shakespeare, Seuss, Twain), medium for their internal order (King vs Rowling vs Shakespeare at #1 is close and depends on fame vs favorite measures). Medium for 6-14: Poe, Dickens and Hemingway are lifted on YouGov fame plus the gut check, against favorite-book polls. Medium-low for 15-24: commercial authors (Steel, Roberts, Grisham, Koontz, Clancy) rest on older Harris polls (2010/2015) and sales; Gabaldon is fan-vote driven. Caveats: Harris author polls only report top 10 and the 2015 positions 4-10 come from a news summary whose page returned 403; no recent general-public favorite-author poll found; Wikipedia pageviews/Google Trends rate-limited and not used; YouGov fame list beyond the top 20 was assembled from per-writer pages (Hoover, Maas, C.S. Lewis, Salinger pages not found).
